targets.summary: The new combine helpers (_sum_combine, _prod_combine, _max_combine, etc.) repeat functionality that already exists in the op overrides; reuse the existing overrides instead.
targets.adoption_evidence: The flagged helper `def _max_combine(lhs, rhs): import cutlass; return cutlass.max(lhs, rhs)` (line 110: `import cutlass`) was deleted in the merged code. The other duplicate helpers went with it (_sum_combine, _prod_combine, _min_combine, the source/finalize helpers, MaterializedTensorSSAReduction and materialize_tensorssa_reduction). The only definition left is the existing string-based descriptor in TENSORSSA_REDUCTIONS: `"max": TensorSSAReduction("cute.ReductionOp.MAX", 'float("-inf")', "cutlass.max(lhs, rhs)")`. So the duplicated combine logic is gone and the existing machinery is used, which is what the maintainer asked for.
targets.stage3_reason: `_max_combine` (`cutlass.max(lhs, rhs)`) and the rest of `materialize_tensorssa_reduction` repeat what the same file already defines in `TENSORSSA_REDUCTIONS` (`combine_expr "cutlass.max(lhs, rhs)"`, `cute.ReductionOp.MAX`, the init values) and in the op overrides. That makes it a second, parallel reduction path, a design problem a reviewer can see from this file alone. The merged code deletes all of these helpers along with `MaterializedTensorSSAReduction`.
